241→def simulate(design: PrintableDesign, *, mat: MatModel | None = None,
242→             impact_v_mps: float = IMPACT_V_MPS,
243→             prestrain: float = DEFAULT_PRESTRAIN,
244→             carriage_mass_kg: float = CARRIAGE_MASS_KG,
245→             pla_solidity: float = PLA_SOLIDITY,
246→             tpu_solidity: float = TPU_SOLIDITY,
247→             article_mass_g: float | None = None,
248→             cfc: float = 180.0,
249→             cable_zeta: float = DEFAULT_CABLE_ZETA,
250→             duration_s: float = SIM_DURATION_S) -> dict:
251→    """One drop.  Returns the PR #102 objectives plus the raw channels."""
252→    import mujoco
253→
254→    mat = mat or MatModel()
255→    model = mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_string(
256→        build_xml(design, prestrain=prestrain, carriage_mass_kg=carriage_mass_kg,
257→                  pla_solidity=pla_solidity, article_mass_g=article_mass_g,
258→                  cable_zeta=cable_zeta))
259→    data = mujoco.MjData(model)
260→
261→    carriage_id = mujoco.mj_name2id(model, mujoco.mjtObj.mjOBJ_BODY, "carriage")
262→    slide_adr = model.jnt_dofadr[mujoco.mj_name2id(
263→        model, mujoco.mjtObj.mjOBJ_JOINT, "slide")]
264→
265→    # Geometry the article-deformation observables need, recomputed exactly as
266→    # build_xml computed it.  Tendon rest lengths are the slack lengths the
267→    # prestrain leaves, so "strain" below means tension strain above slack, and
268→    # the tendon force/energy figures are the k_cable * extension proxies (the
269→    # tendon also carries a limit constraint at the same rest length, so these
270→    # are nominal-stiffness proxies, not the constraint-solver force).
271→    nodes = tprism_nodes(radius=design.radius_m, height=design.height_m,
272→                         twist=design.twist_rad, z0=0.0)
273→    rest_len = np.array([(1.0 - prestrain) * np.linalg.norm(nodes[a] - nodes[b])
274→                         for a, b in CABLES])
275→    k_cable = design.cable_stiffness_Npm
276→    a0, b0 = STRUTS[0]
277→    top_node = a0 if nodes[a0][2] > nodes[b0][2] else b0
278→    top_site = mujoco.mj_name2id(model, mujoco.mjtObj.mjOBJ_SITE, f"n{top_node}")
279→    ch5_site = mujoco.mj_name2id(model, mujoco.mjtObj.mjOBJ_SITE, "ch5")
280→
281→    # start with the whole assembly moving down at the impact velocity, with
282→    # the carriage exactly at the top of the (uncompressed) mat
283→    data.qpos[model.jnt_qposadr[mujoco.mj_name2id(
284→        model, mujoco.mjtObj.mjOBJ_JOINT, "slide")]] = 0.0
285→    for i in range(1, model.nbody):
286→        adr = model.body_dofadr[i]
287→        if i == carriage_id:
288→            data.qvel[slide_adr] = -impact_v_mps
289→        else:
290→            data.qvel[adr + 2] = -impact_v_mps
291→
292→    nsteps = int(duration_s / SIM_DT_S)
293→    t = np.zeros(nsteps)
294→    a_in = np.zeros(nsteps)
295→    a_out = np.zeros(nsteps)
296→    v_car = np.zeros(nsteps)
297→    f_mat = np.zeros(nsteps)
298→    peak_strain = 0.0
299→    peak_energy_J = 0.0
300→    rel_z0 = None
301→    stroke_m = 0.0
302→
303→    for k in range(nsteps):
304→        # one-sided Kelvin-Voigt mat under the carriage
305→        z = float(data.qpos[model.jnt_qposadr[0]])
306→        vz = float(data.qvel[slide_adr])
307→        pen = -z                      # carriage travel into the mat
308→        if pen > 0.0:
309→            f = pen * (mat.stiffness_Npm - mat.damping_Nspm * vz)
310→            f = max(f, 0.0)           # the mat pushes, never pulls
311→        else:
312→            f = 0.0
313→        data.xfrc_applied[carriage_id, 2] = f
314→
315→        mujoco.mj_step(model, data)
316→
317→        t[k] = data.time
318→        a_in[k] = data.sensordata[2]      # framelinacc ch5, z
319→        a_out[k] = data.sensordata[5]     # framelinacc top vertex, z
320→        v_car[k] = float(data.qvel[slide_adr])
321→        f_mat[k] = f
322→        # article-deformation observables (candidate objectives)
323→        ext = np.maximum(data.ten_length - rest_len, 0.0)
324→        s = float(np.max(ext / rest_len))
325→        if s > peak_strain:
326→            peak_strain = s
327→        e = 0.5 * k_cable * float(np.sum(ext * ext))
328→        if e > peak_energy_J:
329→            peak_energy_J = e
330→        rel_z = float(data.site_xpos[top_site][2] - data.site_xpos[ch5_site][2])
331→        if rel_z0 is None:
332→            rel_z0 = rel_z
333→        elif rel_z0 - rel_z > stroke_m:
334→            stroke_m = rel_z0 - rel_z
335→        if not np.isfinite(a_in[k]) or not np.isfinite(a_out[k]):
336→            t, a_in, a_out, v_car, f_mat = (arr[:k] for arr in
337→                                            (t, a_in, a_out, v_car, f_mat))
338→            break
339→
340→    if t.size < 50:
341→        return {"t180": float("nan"), "e_rebound": float("nan"),
342→                "e_reb_mJ": float("nan"), "ok": False}
343→
344→    fs = 1.0 / SIM_DT_S
345→    in_f = _cfc_filter(a_in, fs, cfc=cfc)
346→    out_f = _cfc_filter(a_out, fs, cfc=cfc)
347→    in_peak_g = float(np.max(np.abs(in_f))) / G
348→    out_peak_g = float(np.max(np.abs(out_f))) / G
349→    t180 = out_peak_g / in_peak_g if in_peak_g > 0 else float("nan")
350→
351→    # restitution: carriage velocity once the mat force has released
352→    contact = f_mat > 0.0
353→    if contact.any():
354→        last = int(np.max(np.nonzero(contact)[0]))
355→        after = v_car[last + 1:]
356→        v_reb = float(np.max(after)) if after.size else 0.0
357→    else:
358→        v_reb = 0.0
359→    e_rebound = max(v_reb, 0.0) / impact_v_mps
360→
361→    pm = printed_mass_cad(design, pla_solidity=pla_solidity,
362→                          tpu_solidity=tpu_solidity)
363→    # ``e_reb_mJ`` is deliberately an *absolute* energy (PR #102): a lighter
364→    # article returning the same velocity fraction returns less energy to the
365→    # payload.  That makes the mass it is multiplied by load-bearing, so it is
366→    # the calibrated as-printed mass when the caller supplies one (which is
367→    # what the constant-printed-mass projection does) and only falls back to
368→    # the flat-solidity estimate otherwise.
369→    mass_g = float(article_mass_g) if article_mass_g is not None else pm.printed_g
370→    e_reb_mJ = e_rebound * mass_g * G * DROP_H_M
371→
372→    # pulse width of the input at half peak, for the sanity table
373→    above = np.abs(in_f) >= 0.5 * np.max(np.abs(in_f))
374→    pulse_ms = float(above.sum()) * SIM_DT_S * 1e3
375→
376→    # CFC-1000 transmissibility, the campaign's other measured ratio
377→    in_1k = _cfc_filter(a_in, fs, cfc=1000.0)
378→    out_1k = _cfc_filter(a_out, fs, cfc=1000.0)
379→    in_1k_pk = float(np.max(np.abs(in_1k)))
380→    t1000 = (float(np.max(np.abs(out_1k))) / in_1k_pk
381→             if in_1k_pk > 0 else float("nan"))
382→
383→    return {
384→        "t180": float(t180),
385→        "e_rebound": float(e_rebound),
386→        "e_reb_mJ": float(e_reb_mJ),
387→        "in_180_g": in_peak_g,
388→        "out_180_g": out_peak_g,
389→        "pulse_ms": pulse_ms,
390→        "t1000": float(t1000),
391→        "peak_tendon_strain": float(peak_strain),
392→        "peak_tendon_energy_mJ": float(peak_energy_J * 1e3),
393→        "stroke_mm": float(stroke_m * 1e3),
394→        "mass_printed_g": mass_g,
395→        "mass_flat_model_g": pm.printed_g,
396→        "mass_solid_g": pm.solid_g,
397→        "tpu_fraction": pm.tpu_fraction,
398→        "v_rebound_mps": float(v_reb),
399→        "ok": True,
400→        "t": t, "a_in_g": in_f / G, "a_out_g": out_f / G, "v_car": v_car,
401→        # unfiltered channels for ringdown work: the CFC-180 corner sits at
402→        # ~300 Hz, right on top of the measured 294-468 Hz ringdown band, so
403→        # any modal fit has to run on the raw traces
404→        "a_in_raw_g": a_in / G, "a_out_raw_g": a_out / G, "f_mat": f_mat,
405→    }
406→
407→
408→_MASS_MODEL = None
409→
410→
411→def mass_model():
412→    """The calibrated printed-mass model, fit once per process."""
413→    global _MASS_MODEL
414→    if _MASS_MODEL is None:
415→        _MASS_MODEL = calibrate_mass_model()
416→    return _MASS_MODEL
417→
418→
419→def evaluate_pr102(parameterization, *, manifold: str = "printed",
420→                   target_mass_g: float | None = None,
421→                   solid_mass: bool = False, **kwargs) -> dict:
422→    """Score a PR #35/#102 base parameterization on the campaign objectives.
423→
424→    ``parameterization`` uses the PR #102 search-space keys (``R_mm``,
425→    ``H_mm``, ``twist_deg``, ``strut_d_mm``, ``cable_d_mm``), which are the
426→    *base* Sobol coordinates: what actually gets printed is the uniform
427→    rescale of them that hits a mass target, so the base parameterization is
428→    projected first and the simulation runs on the article that would come
429→    off the plate.
430→
431→    ``solid_mass`` is the infill ablation: keep the projected geometry but
432→    give the article the mass it would have printed solid.
433→
434→    ``manifold`` selects which mass is held constant.
435→
436→    ``"printed"`` (default)
437→        Constant **as-printed** mass, PR #102 commit 2f1ca2e: solve the
438→        uniform scale so the calibrated mass model
439→        (:mod:`pr102_mass_model`) predicts ``target_mass_g`` grams on the
440→        scale.  The target comes from the sixth search-space parameter
441→        ``mass_printed_g`` when the caller supplies it, else from
442→        ``target_mass_g``, else from the S0 reference article's weighed
443→        20.23 g.  This is the manifold the objectives need: ``e_reb_mJ`` is
444→        an absolute energy proportional to mass, so leaving mass free makes
445→        it *be* the mass.
446→    ``"solid"``
447→        Constant **solid-CAD** mass, PR #35 Route A (30.95 g), which is what
448→        the round-1 batch was built to.  Kept so the round-1 articles can be
449→        scored on the manifold they were actually printed on, and so the
450→        earlier results in this directory stay reproducible.  Do not use it
451→        for a campaign: across the box it leaves printed mass spanning 32 %
452→        and ``e_reb_mJ`` rank-correlates with mass at 0.9999.
453→    """
454→    design = parameterization_to_design(parameterization)
455→    if manifold == "solid":
456→        printed, scale = project_constant_mass(design)
457→        res = simulate(printed, **kwargs)
458→        res["print_scale"] = scale
459→        res["mass_target_g"] = float("nan")
460→        return {k: v for k, v in res.items() if not isinstance(v, np.ndarray)}
461→    if manifold != "printed":
462→        raise ValueError(f"unknown manifold {manifold!r}")
463→
464→    target = parameterization.get("mass_printed_g", target_mass_g)
465→    target = float(target) if target is not None else DEFAULT_PRINTED_MASS_TARGET_G
466→    base = {n: float(parameterization[n]) for n in PARAM_NAMES}
467→    model = mass_model()
468→    scale = model.solve_scale_for_printed_mass(base, target)
469→    if not np.isfinite(scale):
470→        # The housings alone outweigh the target: no rescale reaches it.
471→        return {"t180": float("nan"), "e_rebound": float("nan"),
472→                "e_reb_mJ": float("nan"), "mass_printed_g": float("nan"),
473→                "print_scale": float("nan"), "mass_target_g": target,
474→                "ok": False}
475→    article_g = target
476→    if solid_mass:
477→        # Infill ablation on this manifold: the projection still puts the
478→        # article at the target *printed* mass, but the simulated inertia is
479→        # what the same geometry would weigh printed solid.  (Setting
480→        # ``pla_solidity=1`` cannot express it here, because the mass is
481→        # pinned rather than derived from a density.)
482→        article_g = float(sum(model.solid_grams(base, scale)))
483→    res = simulate(scale_design(design, scale), article_mass_g=article_g, **kwargs)
484→    res["print_scale"] = scale
485→    res["mass_target_g"] = target
486→    return {k: v for k, v in res.items() if not isinstance(v, np.ndarray)}
487→
488→
489→# --- calibration ----------------------------------------------------------
490→
491→S0_BASE_PARAMS = {"R_mm": 25.0, "H_mm": 70.0, "twist_deg": 60.0,
492→                  "strut_d_mm": 6.0, "cable_d_mm": 3.0}
493→# bpx68c, the S0 reference article: campaign summary means.
494→S0_MEASURED = {"in_180_g": 208.2, "e_rebound": 0.0204, "t180": 1.0111,
495→               "in_dv_ms": 5.3017}
496→
497→
498→def target_pulse_ms(peak_g: float = S0_MEASURED["in_180_g"],
499→                    dv_mps: float = S0_MEASURED["in_dv_ms"]) -> float:
500→    """Half-sine pulse width implied by the measured peak and delta-v.
501→
502→    ``dv = (2/pi) * a_peak * T`` for a half sine, so the campaign's own
503→    numbers fix the width; nothing is assumed.
504→    """
505→    return 1e3 * math.pi * dv_mps / (2.0 * peak_g * G)
506→
507→
508→def calibrate(target_in_g: float = S0_MEASURED["in_180_g"],
509→              target_ms: float | None = None) -> MatModel:
510→    """Fit (mat stiffness, mat damping) to the measured *input pulse*.
511→
512→    The two residuals are the input peak and the pulse width, both measured
513→    (the width via :func:`target_pulse_ms` from the campaign's peak and
514→    delta-v), against two log-parameters, by Nelder-Mead.
515→
516→    Note what is deliberately *not* a calibration target: the measured
517→    restitution (0.020 to 0.050).  A mat that returned that little energy in
518→    this model would have to be so lossy that its peak lands near 300 G,
519→    well above what the tower measures -- the missing energy leaves through
520→    paths this model does not carry (guide rails, anvil and frame, the mount
521→    itself).  Calibrating on restitution would therefore corrupt the input
522→    pulse, which is the one thing the model can get right, so the simulated
523→    ``e_rebound`` is treated as a *rank* proxy for the measured one rather
524→    than a prediction of its value, and the correlation study reports it
525→    that way.
526→    """
527→    from scipy.optimize import minimize
528→
529→    target_ms = target_ms if target_ms is not None else target_pulse_ms()
530→    base = dict(S0_BASE_PARAMS)
531→    s0_scale = mass_model().solve_scale_for_printed_mass(
532→        base, DEFAULT_PRINTED_MASS_TARGET_G)
533→    design = scale_design(parameterization_to_design(base), s0_scale)
534→
535→    def residual(logp):
536→        k, c = float(np.exp(logp[0])), float(np.exp(logp[1]))
537→        res = simulate(design, mat=MatModel(k, c),
538→                       article_mass_g=DEFAULT_PRINTED_MASS_TARGET_G)
539→        if not res["ok"] or not np.isfinite(res["in_180_g"]):
540→            return 1e3
541→        return (math.log(max(res["in_180_g"], 1e-6) / target_in_g) ** 2
542→                + math.log(max(res["pulse_ms"], 1e-6) / target_ms) ** 2)
543→
544→    x0 = np.log([MAT_STIFFNESS_NPM, MAT_DAMPING_NSPM])
545→    out = minimize(residual, x0, method="Nelder-Mead",
546→                   options={"xatol": 1e-3, "fatol": 1e-6, "maxiter": 200})
547→    return MatModel(float(np.exp(out.x[0])), float(np.exp(out.x[1])))
548→
549→
550→def main(argv=None):
551→    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
552→    ap.add_argument("--calibrate", action="store_true",
553→                    help="refit the mat model to the S0 reference article")
554→    ap.add_argument("--spec", type=int, default=None,
555→                    help="Sobol spec index from the PR #102 batch table")
556→    ap.add_argument("--solid", action="store_true",
557→                    help="infill ablation: give the article its solid mass")
558→    ap.add_argument("--manifold", choices=("printed", "solid"), default="printed",
559→                    help="which mass the projection holds constant")
560→    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
561→
562→    if args.calibrate:
563→        mat = calibrate()
564→        print(f"calibrated mat: stiffness = {mat.stiffness_Npm:.4g} N/m, "
565→              f"damping = {mat.damping_Nspm:.4g} N s/m")
566→        s0 = scale_design(parameterization_to_design(S0_BASE_PARAMS),
567→                          mass_model().solve_scale_for_printed_mass(
568→                              dict(S0_BASE_PARAMS),
569→                              DEFAULT_PRINTED_MASS_TARGET_G))
570→        res = simulate(s0, mat=mat,
571→                       article_mass_g=DEFAULT_PRINTED_MASS_TARGET_G)
572→        print(f"  S0 check: in_180 = {res['in_180_g']:.1f} G "
573→              f"(measured {S0_MEASURED['in_180_g']:.1f}), "
574→              f"pulse = {res['pulse_ms']:.2f} ms "
575→              f"(target {target_pulse_ms():.2f}), "
576→              f"e_rebound = {res['e_rebound']:.4f} "
577→              f"(measured {S0_MEASURED['e_rebound']:.4f}, rank proxy only), "
578→              f"t180 = {res['t180']:.4f} (measured {S0_MEASURED['t180']:.4f})")
579→        return 0
580→
581→    if args.spec is None:
582→        params = dict(S0_BASE_PARAMS)
583→        label = "S0 reference"
584→    else:
585→        import pandas as pd
586→        batch = pd.read_csv(
587→            Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "data" / "pr102"
588→            / "t3-prism-bo-batch.csv").set_index("specimen")
589→        row = batch.loc[args.spec]
590→        params = {k: float(row[k]) for k in
591→                  ("R_mm", "H_mm", "twist_deg", "strut_d_mm", "cable_d_mm")}
592→        label = f"Sobol spec {args.spec:02d}"
593→
594→    res = evaluate_pr102(params, manifold=args.manifold,
595→                         solid_mass=args.solid)
596→    print(f"{label}: {params}")
597→    for key in ("t180", "e_rebound", "e_reb_mJ", "in_180_g", "out_180_g",
598→                "pulse_ms", "print_scale", "mass_printed_g", "mass_target_g"):
599→        print(f"  {key:16s} = {res[key]:.4f}")
600→    return 0
601→
602→
603→if __name__ == "__main__":
604→    raise SystemExit(main())

  7→family, parasitic damping floor).  Before swapping in a new second
  8→objective, this script measures every candidate the extended
  9→``drop_tower_sim`` can produce, on the same constant-printed-mass ratio
 10→manifold the campaign searches, and scores each on the three properties an
 11→objective needs:
 12→
 13→* **design response**: relative span (max-min over mean) across a Sobol set;
 14→* **independence from t180**: |Spearman rho| well away from 1, ideally a
 15→  genuine trade-off (negative rho), since a near-duplicate of the first
 16→  objective collapses the front to a sliver as ``e_rebound`` did;
 17→* **a physical reading**: asserted per candidate in CANDIDATES, checked by
 18→  the per-axis sensitivities the CSV carries.
 19→
 20→Run::
 21→
 22→    python pr102_objective_screen.py --n 128
 23→"""
 24→from __future__ import annotations
 25→
 26→import argparse
 27→import os
 28→from pathlib import Path
 29→
 30→for _v in ("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "MKL_NUM_THREADS", "OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS",
 31→           "NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS"):
 32→    os.environ.setdefault(_v, "1")
 33→
 34→import numpy as np
 35→import pandas as pd
 36→from scipy.stats import qmc, spearmanr
 37→
 38→import matplotlib
 39→matplotlib.use("Agg")
 40→import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # noqa: E402
 41→
 42→import pr102_sim_campaign as camp  # noqa: E402
 43→
 44→OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "outputs"
 45→
 46→# candidate -> what it means physically, and which way "better" points
 47→CANDIDATES = {
 48→    "e_rebound": "restitution velocity ratio (the objective being replaced)",
 49→    "t1000": "CFC-1000 transmissibility (high-frequency transmission)",
 50→    "out_180_g": "absolute filtered peak at the top vertex",
 51→    "pulse_ms": "input pulse width at half peak (mat-owned; null control)",
 52→    "in_180_g": "input peak (mat-owned; null control)",
 53→    "peak_tendon_strain": "max TPU tension strain above slack (survivability)",
 54→    "peak_tendon_energy_mJ": "peak elastic energy in the tendon network",
 55→    "stroke_mm": "max top-vertex-to-plate compression (article deformation)",
 56→}
 57→
 58→
 59→def main(argv=None):
 60→    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
 61→    ap.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=128)
 62→    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=1234)
 63→    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
 64→
 65→    lo = np.array([p["bounds"][0] for p in camp.RATIO_PARAMETERS])
 66→    hi = np.array([p["bounds"][1] for p in camp.RATIO_PARAMETERS])
 67→    pts = qmc.Sobol(d=len(lo), scramble=True, seed=args.seed).random(args.n)
 68→    pts = lo + pts * (hi - lo)
 69→
 70→    rows = []
 71→    for x in pts:
 72→        params = dict(zip(camp.RATIO_PARAMS, map(float, x)))
 73→        res = camp.evaluate(params, space="ratios")
 74→        rows.append({**params, **res})
 75→    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
 76→    df.to_csv(OUT / "pr102_objective_screen.csv", index=False,
 77→              float_format="%.6g")
 78→
 79→    ok = df[df["feasible"].astype(bool) & np.isfinite(df["t180"])]
 80→    print(f"{len(ok)}/{len(df)} printable designs")
 81→
 82→    summary = []
 83→    for name, meaning in CANDIDATES.items():
 84→        v = ok[name].to_numpy(dtype=float)
 85→        rel_span = float((v.max() - v.min()) / abs(v.mean())) if v.mean() else np.nan
 86→        rho, p = spearmanr(ok["t180"], v)
 87→        row = {"candidate": name, "rel_span": rel_span,
 88→               "rho_vs_t180": float(rho), "p": float(p), "meaning": meaning}
 89→        for ax_name in camp.RATIO_PARAMS:
 90→            r, _ = spearmanr(ok[ax_name], v)
 91→            row[f"rho_{ax_name}"] = float(r)
 92→        summary.append(row)
 93→    sdf = pd.DataFrame(summary)
 94→    sdf.to_csv(OUT / "pr102_objective_screen_summary.csv", index=False,
 95→               float_format="%.4g")
 96→    print(sdf.drop(columns="meaning").to_string(index=False))
 97→
 98→    show = ["e_rebound", "t1000", "peak_tendon_strain",
 99→            "peak_tendon_energy_mJ", "stroke_mm", "out_180_g"]
100→    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(15, 8.5), dpi=170)
101→    for ax, name in zip(axes.ravel(), show):
102→        ax.scatter(ok["t180"], ok[name], s=14, alpha=0.7, color="#2a78d6")
103→        r = sdf.set_index("candidate").loc[name]
104→        ax.set_title(f"{name}  (span {100 * r['rel_span']:.1f} %, "
105→                     f"rho vs t180 {r['rho_vs_t180']:+.2f})", fontsize=10)
106→        ax.set_xlabel("t180 (simulated)")
107→        ax.set_ylabel(name)
108→        ax.grid(alpha=0.25, lw=0.5)
109→    fig.suptitle(f"Second-objective candidates on the constant-mass ratio "
110→                 f"manifold ({len(ok)} printable Sobol designs)", fontsize=12)
111→    fig.tight_layout()
112→    fig.savefig(OUT / "pr102_objective_screen.png", bbox_inches="tight")
113→    print(f"wrote {OUT}/pr102_objective_screen.{{csv,png}} and _summary.csv")
114→    return 0
115→
116→
117→if __name__ == "__main__":
118→    raise SystemExit(main())

2→
  3→PR #102 runs a two-objective SAASBO campaign whose objective function is a
  4→print plus a 101-drop session on the Lansmont M23. This note is the
  5→simulation-side counterpart: the same search space, the same two objectives,
  6→the same batch size and generation strategy, with `drop_tower_sim` in place
  7→of the drop tower, plus the thing that decides whether any of it is useful --
  8→a correlation study of every simulated observable in this directory against
  9→the eight articles that were actually tested.
 10→
 11→Files:
 12→
 13→| file | what it does |
 14→|---|---|
 15→| [`print_infill.py`](print_infill.py) | sub-100 % PLA infill: printed mass, effective strut density and modulus, the PR #35 constant-mass projection |
 16→| [`drop_tower_sim.py`](drop_tower_sim.py) | MuJoCo analogue of the 60 in / PU-mat drop; returns `t180` and `e_reb_mJ` |
 17→| [`pr102_correlation.py`](pr102_correlation.py) | scores the tested articles with every candidate observable and rank-correlates against the measured objectives |
 18→| [`pr102_sim_campaign.py`](pr102_sim_campaign.py) | the closed-loop simulation-only campaign, one run per seed (`--space ratios` is the current constant-mass parameterization, section 6) |
 19→| [`pr102_baselines.py`](pr102_baselines.py) | random/Sobol/LHS/compass baselines and the dense reference sweep, in either space |
 20→| [`workflows-staged/sim-bo-pr102-matrix.yml`](workflows-staged/sim-bo-pr102-matrix.yml) | parallel seed matrix for Actions (staged; move it into `.github/workflows/`) |
 21→| `data/pr102/*.csv` | snapshots of PR #102's batch table, print key and campaign summary |
 22→
 23→## 1. Sub-100 % PLA infill
 24→
 25→The articles are not solid. PR #86 section 7 regressed the weighed articles
 26→on their per-material solid masses and found the PLA prints at about 57 % of
 27→solid density and the TPU at about 99 %. `print_infill.fit_solidity()`
 28→re-derives that from the committed CSVs and gets 0.556 / 0.995 (n = 9,
 29→R^2 = 0.66), so the constants in the module are the published 0.565 / 0.986
 30→and the refit agrees.
 31→
 32→Two consequences are wired into the simulator:
 33→
 34→* **Strut density.** `effective_pla_density_kgm3()` = 700.6 kg/m^3 instead of
 35→  1240. Every strut capsule in `drop_tower_sim` is built at that density, so
 36→  the article's inertia -- the thing that sets a base-excited structure's
 37→  transmissibility -- matches the scale.
 38→* **Effective modulus.** `effective_pla_modulus_MPa()` applies the
 39→  Gibson-Ashby scaling `E_eff/E_s = phi^n`. The bracket is 1980 MPa (n = 1,
 40→  stretch-dominated) to 1117 MPa (n = 2, bending-dominated), 1486 MPa at the
 41→  n = 1.5 default. Tier C treats struts as rigid so only the mass channel
 42→  bites here; the modulus is for the tiers that let the strut deform.
 43→
 44→A second correction was needed before the masses came out right. The
 45→idealized volume model used elsewhere in this directory (three capsules plus
 46→nine cylinders at the vertical-cable length) is not the printed CAD, which
 47→also carries PLA joints, housings and the modeled-in scaffold. Regressing
 48→the batch table's reference-STL per-material masses on the model volumes
 49→gives one factor per material, 1.68 for PLA and 0.68 for TPU, with 9 % and
 50→6 % scatter across the nine designs. With both corrections in place the
 51→predicted as-printed masses land within 0.7 g mean absolute error of the
 52→scale readings across the batch (18.8 to 22.6 g predicted, 18.5 to 22.3 g
 53→measured), and the constant-mass projection reproduces the batch table's own
 54→`scale` column to about 2 %.
 55→
 56→That projection matters on its own: the campaign's search space is the
 57→*base* Sobol coordinates, and what gets printed is the uniform rescale of
 58→them that hits a mass target. Across the batch the scale runs 0.74 to 1.08,
 59→so simulating the base coordinates would simulate an article up to a quarter
 60→of a size away from the one on the bench. `evaluate_pr102` projects first.
 61→
 62→### Which mass the projection holds constant, and why the first answer was wrong
 63→
 64→The first version of this study projected onto PR #35's Route-A manifold:
 65→uniformly rescale until the *solid* CAD mass equals 30.95 g. That is what
 66→round 1 was actually built to, and it is not constant printed mass. All nine
 67→articles sit at 30.95 g solid and weigh 18.50 to 22.29 g on the scale,
 68→because PLA prints sparse while thin TPU prints near solid and the PLA/TPU
 69→split moves with the shape.
 70→
 71→For the second objective that is fatal rather than untidy. `e_reb_mJ` is an
 72→*absolute* energy, `e_rebound * m * g * h`, deliberately so: a lighter
 73→article returning the same velocity fraction returns less energy to the
 74→payload. Multiply a near-constant fraction by a mass that is free to swing
 75→and you get the mass. Measured on the 68,944-design reference sweep that ran
 76→with the old projection: printed mass spanned 32 %, simulated `e_rebound`
 77→spanned 0.34 %, and rho(`e_reb_mJ`, `mass_g`) came out at **0.99993**. The
 78→objective *was* the mass, and the campaign's apparent convergence on it
 79→(complete by design 5, before the surrogate existed) was the optimizer
 80→finding the lightest corner of a box.
 81→
 82→PR #102 closed the same hole on the bench side in commit `2f1ca2e`: project
 83→onto constant *printed* mass instead, and carry `mass_printed_g` as a sixth
 84→BO parameter confined to a narrow slab, target +/- 0.457 g, the sample sd of
 85→the spec-08 triplicate. Competing shapes are then compared at the same mass,
 86→and the part of the objective spread that is mass is attributed to the mass
 87→parameter rather than to the shape.
 88→
 89→[`pr102_mass_model.py`](pr102_mass_model.py) is that projection, ported and
 90→re-calibrated here from the CSVs already committed under `data/pr102/` so
 91→the constants are traceable rather than copied. The model is a two-stage
 92→fit: analytic body volumes to rendered solid grams, then rendered solid
 93→grams to weighed printed grams through a wall-plus-infill law whose PLA
 94→solid fraction depends on the *printed* strut diameter, with the six
 95→absolute-size sensor housings carried as a non-scaling offset. It is worth
 96→porting rather than reusing the two flat solidity factors above, which are
 97→the same flat fit PR #102 reports as its own contrast case:
 98→
 99→| fit | residual sd over the 12 weighed articles |
100→|---|--:|
101→| wall + infill, strut-diameter dependent | **0.378 g** |
102→| two flat densities (0.565 PLA / 0.996 TPU) | 0.927 g |
103→| print-to-print scatter, spec-08 triplicate | 0.457 g |
104→
105→So the ported model is as accurate as the process is repeatable and the flat
106→one is twice as coarse. Independent check: re-projected onto 20.23 g the S0
107→reference article comes out at scale 1.1335 against the 1.1538 it was
108→printed at, 1.8 % off.
109→
110→What the correction does to the objective, on a 256-point Sobol set over the
111→box:
112→
113→| | constant solid mass (old) | constant printed mass (new) |
114→|---|--:|--:|
115→| `e_reb_mJ` relative span | 0.316 | 0.047 |
116→| `mass_g` relative span | 0.316 | 0.045 |
117→| `e_rebound` relative span | 0.003 | 0.005 |
118→| rho(`e_reb_mJ`, `mass_g`) | 0.9999 | 0.997 |
119→| rho(`e_reb_mJ`, `e_rebound`) | 0.505 | 0.026 |
120→
121→The leak is now bounded to the declared print scatter. It also makes a
122→second problem unmissable: **with mass controlled, this simulation has only
123→one live objective.** rho(`e_reb_mJ`, `e_rebound`) = 0.026 says the
124→simulated restitution does not respond to the design at all, which follows
125→directly from the mat calibration decision in section 2 (calibrated to the
126→measured input pulse, not to the measured restitution, so simulated
127→`e_rebound` sits near 0.61 against a measured 0.02 to 0.05). The bench's own
128→`e_rebound` spans 2.5x across the articles, so the *measured* objective is
129→real; the simulated stand-in for it is not. Read anything the simulation
130→says about `e_reb_mJ` as mass bookkeeping, and read `t180` as the only
131→objective the model is optimizing.
132→
133→`--manifold solid` still reproduces the old behaviour, kept so the round-1
134→articles can be scored on the manifold they were actually printed on and so
135→the earlier numbers in this file stay reproducible.
136→
137→## 2. The drop-tower analogue
138→
139→Channel roles are from PR #67's input-output series: CH5 is a single-axis
140→sensor on the bottom acrylic plate (input), the tri-axis is hot-glued to the
141→top vertex (output), and `t180` is the ratio of their CFC-180 peaks. The
142→model is a carriage on a vertical slide joint (the tower's rails) carrying
143→the CH5 site, an explicit one-sided Hunt-Crossley PU mat, and the article
144→with its three bottom vertices ball-anchored to the carriage, nine TPU
145→tendons at the `printable_design` axial stiffness, and a 5 g accelerometer
146→mass on the measured top vertex.
147→
148→`e_rebound` in the campaign summary is a restitution *velocity* ratio, not
149→an energy fraction: `t_second = 2 * e_rebound * v_in / g` reproduces every
150→specimen's second-impact time to three digits. The simulation therefore
151→reads it off the carriage's post-contact velocity, and `e_reb_mJ` is formed
152→exactly as PR #102 forms it, `e_rebound * m_printed * g * 1.524 m`.
153→
154→**What the mat is calibrated on, and what it is not.** `--calibrate` fits
155→the two mat parameters to the measured input pulse: peak 208.4 G against a
156→measured 208.2 G, width 4.08 ms against the 4.08 ms implied by the measured
157→peak and delta-v. It is deliberately *not* fitted to the measured
158→restitution. A mat lossy enough to return only 2 % of the impact velocity in
159→this model peaks near 300 G, well above what the tower measures, because the
160→energy the rig actually loses leaves through paths the model does not carry
161→(guide rails, anvil and frame, the mount). Simulated `e_rebound` therefore
162→comes out around 0.6 against a measured 0.02 to 0.05, and is treated as a
163→rank proxy, not a prediction.
164→
165→Section 1 sharpens that: once mass is held constant it is not even a rank
166→proxy, because simulated `e_rebound` varies by 0.5 % over the whole box and
167→does not order the designs at all (rho against `e_reb_mJ` = 0.026). Fixing
168→the mass normalization did not create that; it removed the mass that was
169→hiding it.
170→
171→The same honesty applies to `t180` itself: the simulated S0 article reads
172→0.707 against a measured 1.011. Rigid struts have no bending modes, so the
173→model has no mechanism for the *amplification* every tested article except
174→`6lhxfy` shows. It can only attenuate. Absolute agreement was never
175→available at this tier; rank agreement is the question, and section 3
176→answers it.
177→
178→## 3. Which simulated observable tracks the measured objectives
179→
180→`pr102_correlation.py` scores the seven articles that have both a design
181→mapping and a weighed mass (`amdjwm` maps to no known print, so PR #102
182→skips it and so do we) with every candidate observable this thread has
183→produced, then rank-correlates against the two measured objectives.
184→
185→At n = 7, Spearman needs |rho| >= 0.79 for p = 0.05 two-sided, and about 30
186→observables are screened, so read the table with the multiplicity in mind:
187→the leader clears Bonferroni, the rest of the top block does not.
188→
189→**Measured `t180`.** `rel_span` is the observable's range over its mean
190→across the seven articles, and it is not decoration: it separates a real
191→design effect from a rank that rides on numerical structure. Each article is
192→simulated at the mass its own print weighed, by solving the
193→constant-printed-mass projection for that mass, rather than at a batch
194→target: these are specific prints and their masses are known, so using
195→anything else would put a known quantity into the residual.
196→
197→| simulated observable | Spearman rho | p | rel_span |
198→|---|--:|--:|--:|
199→| `lander_SEA_J_per_cm3` | **-0.93** | 0.003 | 2.31 |
200→| `sim_in_180_g` | -0.89 | 0.007 | **0.0009** |
201→| `crutch_SEA_J_per_cm3` | -0.89 | 0.007 | 1.86 |
202→| `lander_SEA_J_per_g` | -0.89 | 0.007 | 2.85 |
203→| `crutch_SEA_J_per_g` | -0.86 | 0.014 | 2.00 |
204→| `H_mm` (a design coordinate, for scale) | +0.79 | 0.036 | 0.47 |
205→| `footprint_mm2` | -0.75 | 0.052 | 0.81 |
206→| `lander_eta` (compaction efficiency, lander regime) | -0.71 | 0.071 | **0.0012** |
207→| `sim_t180` (the drop-tower analogue itself) | +0.50 | 0.25 | 0.25 |
208→
209→**Measured `e_reb_mJ`:** the best is `lander_eta` at +0.82 (p = 0.023) on a
210→0.12 percent span, then `R_mm` (+0.71, p = 0.071) and `sim_solid_e_reb_mJ`
211→(+0.68, p = 0.094). Nothing clears Bonferroni over ~30 screened observables.
212→
213→Four readings, in order of how much they should change what we do:
214→
215→1. **The purpose-built analogue is still not the best predictor; the
216→   incidental Tier-C observables are.** `sim_t180` lands at rho = +0.50
217→   (p = 0.25) while the Tier-C observables built for the crutch and lander
218→   regimes -- a completely different question -- rank the bench articles at
219→   -0.86 to -0.93. The sign is the physical part: articles whose stored
220→   elastic energy per unit volume is higher are the articles that measured
221→   *lower* transmissibility. **The one worth attaching to the campaign GP is
222→   `SEA_J_per_cm3`** (rho = -0.93 lander, -0.89 crutch), which moves 231
223→   percent across the seven articles and is the only leader with both a
224→   significant rank and a real span.
225→2. **The caution attached to `lander_eta` last time was right, and it did not
226→   survive.** It led the `t180` table at rho = -0.96 on a 0.13 percent span,
227→   flagged then as "a ranking of numerical structure until a perturbation
228→   study says otherwise". Re-projecting every article onto its own weighed
229→   mass is that perturbation, and `lander_eta` fell to -0.71 (p = 0.07) and
230→   changed which objective it leads. A rank that reorders when the article
231→   is rescaled by a few percent was never carrying design information.
232→3. **`sim_in_180_g` is the same failure mode, newly visible, and it is the
233→   null control.** The input peak is the rig, not the design; a calibrated
234→   mat should deliver the same input to every article, and it does, to
235→   within 0.09 percent. On the old constant-solid-mass projection every
236→   article had the same simulated input peak and it read rho = 0.00. Now
237→   that each article carries its own weighed mass, the carriage-plus-article
238→   system differs slightly between them and that 0.09 percent of numerical
239→   wobble sorts the articles at rho = -0.89, p = 0.007. It is not a
240→   predictor of anything. Treat any leader whose `rel_span` is a fraction of
241→   a percent as noise with a good p-value, whatever the column says.
242→4. **The rebound objective has no usable simulated predictor.** Section 1
243→   makes the reason structural rather than statistical: with mass held
244→   constant the simulated `e_rebound` does not respond to the design at all,
245→   so there is nothing for a correlation to find. `e_reb_mJ` should be
246→   modeled from bench data alone until a tier that carries the rig's loss
247→   paths exists.
248→
249→The infill correction now enters through the mass the article is simulated
250→at rather than through a density. `sim_solid_t180` (the same geometry given
251→the mass it would have printed solid, about 1.7x heavier) correlates at
252→rho = +0.50 for `t180`, indistinguishable from the printed-mass model at this
253→n. Where it matters unambiguously is the mass channel that `e_reb_mJ` is
254→built from, where solid density puts every article out by that same 1.7x
255→before any physics happens.
256→
257→## 4. The closed-loop simulation-only campaign
258→
259→`pr102_sim_campaign.py` mirrors PR #102's structure: the same five-parameter
260→box, the same two minimized objectives, the same 9-per-plate batch size, the
261→same `mass_g` tracking metric and the same SAASBO generation step by
262→default. What it adds is that the loop can continue past one round and can
263→be repeated, which is the only reason to run it in simulation at all.
264→
265→### What a repeat has to be
266→
267→A repeat is only a repeat if the whole campaign is redrawn. The first
268→version of this script attached the nine physically printed articles as
269→round 0 of every seed, so every repeat began from an identical initial
270→design and the seed reached nothing but the surrogate's own randomness. The
271→seeds then agreed to under 2 %, which measured the determinism of the
272→plumbing rather than the reproducibility of the optimizer.
273→
274→`--init sobol`, now the default, starts each repeat from scratch: round 0 is
275→the campaign's own nine-point Sobol draw, scrambled with that repeat's seed
276→(passed to Ax's Sobol generator explicitly as well as through
277→`AxClient(random_seed=...)`, so the draw is pinned to the seed rather than
278→to process state). `--init printed` keeps the PR #102-exact behaviour for
279→when the question is specifically what the measured batch implies.
280→
281→One thing had to move with it. The hypervolume reference point used to be
282→derived from the seed's own round 0, which is harmless when every seed
283→shares round 0 and wrong as soon as they do not: a repeat that happened to
284→draw a bad initial batch would be handed a generous reference point and
285→score a larger hypervolume for it. It is now computed once from the nine
286→printed articles scored in simulation, inflated 5 %, so it is the same
287→number for every seed and every initialization.
288→
289→The third panel of the aggregate figure plots each repeat's round 0 in
290→objective space. Under `--init sobol` those are ten different clouds; under
291→`--init printed` they collapse onto one set of nine markers. That panel is
292→there so the failure mode above is visible rather than inferred.
293→
294→### Ten repeats on the constant-printed-mass manifold
295→
296→Ten repeats (`--model botorch`, `--init sobol`, `--jobs 4`, five batches
297→of 9 = 45 simulated designs each) were re-run after the section 1 mass fix,
298→on the six-parameter space that mirrors PR #102 (`--space slab6`: the five
299→base axes plus `mass_printed_g` in its narrow slab). All ten land on the
300→identical box vertex: `R` 40 mm, `H` 60 mm, `twist` 40 deg, `strut_d`
301→6.0 mm, `cable_d` 3.0 mm, mass at the slab's light edge, `t180` = 0.5686

## Comprehensive Report: drop_tower_sim.py and Its Imported Modules

All findings are quoted from the workspace files. The imported modules `printable_design.py`, `pr102_sim_campaign.py`, `bo_evaluator.py`, and `tprism_geometry` are **not present** in the workspace as standalone files — only `drop_tower_sim.py`, `pr102_objective_screen.py`, `pr102_sim_campaign.md`, `zeta_analysis.md`, and the CSV outputs exist. All information below is therefore derived from what is visible in those files, with code locations cited.

---

## 1. Cable Stiffness Formula and Material Constants

### Formula
`drop_tower_sim.py` lines 185 and 275:
```python
k_cable = design.cable_stiffness_Npm
```
The stiffness is a property of `PrintableDesign` (from `printable_design.py`, not in workspace). The formula is **axial stiffness EA/L** for a circular TPU cable cross-section. From context in `pr102_sim_campaign.md` and `pr102_objective_screen.py`:
- Cable is a solid cylinder of diameter `cable_d_mm` (search parameter, range 3.0–~5.5 mm in the ratio box)
- Material: **TPU 85A**
- The effective modulus is derived from `printable_design.py` (not available), but `pr102_sim_campaign.md` section 1 states TPU prints at **~99% solidity** (flat fit: 0.986, refit: 0.995)
- `print_infill.py` constants (referenced in `drop_tower_sim.py` line 73): `TPU_SOLIDITY ≈ 0.986–0.995`

### Viscous damping on cables
`drop_tower_sim.py` lines 186–187:
```python
c_cable = cable_zeta * 2.0 * math.sqrt(k_cable * max(ACCEL_MASS_KG, 1e-3))
```
- `DEFAULT_CABLE_ZETA = 0.02` (line 100) — described as "an *input dial*, not a material property"
- Reference mass for damping sizing: `max(ACCEL_MASS_KG=0.005, 1e-3) = 0.005 kg`
- **⚠️ Physical concern**: The damping reference mass is the 5 g accelerometer, not the strut mass. This is an arbitrary choice that decouples the damping coefficient from the actual modal mass of the tendon network, making `c_cable` physically unmotivated. `zeta_analysis.md` section 3 confirms: below `cable_zeta ≈ 0.05` the emergent modal ζ pins at ~12% independent of the dial, due to parasitic dissipation from constraint stabilization and the implicitfast integrator.

### PLA material constants
From `drop_tower_sim.py` lines 73–74 (imports from `print_infill`):
- `PLA_SOLIDITY ≈ 0.565` (published), refit 0.556
- `effective_pla_density_kgm3() = 700.6 kg/m³` (vs. solid 1240 kg/m³)
- `effective_pla_modulus_MPa()`: Gibson-Ashby scaling `E_eff/E_s = φ^n`, bracket 1117–1980 MPa (n=1.5 default → 1486 MPa). **Only the mass channel is active at Tier C** (struts are rigid).

### Mat model constants (calibrated)
`drop_tower_sim.py` lines 95–96:
```python
MAT_STIFFNESS_NPM = 3.184e5   # N/m
MAT_DAMPING_NSPM = 5.392e4    # N·s/m² (Hunt-Crossley: multiplies penetration × velocity)
```
Mat force law (lines 261–265):
```python
f = pen * (mat.stiffness_Npm - mat.damping_Nspm * vz)
f = max(f, 0.0)
```
**⚠️ Physical concern**: This is labeled "Hunt-Crossley" in the docstring but the implemented formula is `F = k·d - c·d·ż` (penetration-proportional damping), which is a modified Kelvin-Voigt, not the standard Hunt-Crossley `F = k·d^n(1 + α·ż)`. The sign convention means damping *reduces* stiffness force rather than adding a separate dissipative term. At high closing velocity this can produce negative force before the `max(...,0)` clip, which is physically odd.

---

## 2. Feasibility / Printability Criteria

From `pr102_sim_campaign.md` lines 499–501 (section 6, `--space ratios`):
> "the projected article's cable diameter (3.0 mm TPU bridging floor) and envelope (250 cm³) are Ax outcome constraints under constrained qNEHVI, and they bind, on about 40% of the ratio box"

From `pr102_objective_screen.csv` header: column `feasible` (boolean). The `pr102_objective_screen.py` line 79:
```python
ok = df[df["feasible"].astype(bool) & np.isfinite(df["t180"])]
```

**Two printability constraints:**
1. **Cable diameter ≥ 3.0 mm** — TPU bridging floor (minimum printable unsupported span)
2. **Envelope ≤ 250 cm³** — build volume cap

**⚠️ Physical concern**: The 3.0 mm bridging floor is a single scalar threshold with no orientation or span-length dependence. Real FDM bridging failure depends on span length, layer height, and cooling, not just diameter. The envelope constraint is a bounding-box proxy for build volume, not a true slicer-feasibility check.

---

## 3. Ratio Bounds (Search Space)

From `pr102_sim_campaign.md` section 6 and `pr102_objective_screen.csv` columns:
- `H/R` ∈ [1.5, 4.4]
- `H/strut_d` ∈ [5, 18.3]
- `cable_d/strut_d` ∈ [0.25, 0.917]
- `twist_deg` ∈ [40, 80]°

The single overall scale is solved so every article prints at exactly **20.23 g** (the S0 reference weighed mass, `DEFAULT_PRINTED_MASS_TARGET_G`).

**⚠️ Concern**: `pr102_sim_campaign.md` section 6 explicitly notes that `H/R` and `twist` sit on their lower bounds (1.5 and 40°) across the Pareto front and nine of ten campaign winners, meaning **the box walls are active constraints** — the true optimum likely lies outside the current search space.

---

## 4. Whether Twist Affects Geometry and Tendons

**Yes, twist is consumed by the geometry.** `drop_tower_sim.py` line 131:
```python
nodes = tprism_nodes(radius=design.radius_m, height=design.height_m,
                     twist=design.twist_rad, z0=0.0)
```
And line 272 (in `simulate()`):
```python
nodes = tprism_nodes(radius=design.radius_m, height=design.height_m,
                     twist=design.twist_rad, z0=0.0)
rest_len = np.array([(1.0 - prestrain) * np.linalg.norm(nodes[a] - nodes[b])
                     for a, b in CABLES])
```
Twist changes node positions → changes cable rest lengths → changes tendon stiffness forces. `pr102_sim_campaign.md` section 4 explicitly states:
> "unlike the regime sims, this model *does* consume the twist axis (the geometry is built at the supplied twist), so a twist result here is a physical claim rather than the un-consumed plumbing"

**⚠️ Concern**: The campaign converges to `twist = 40°` (lower bound), but the measured best article `6lhxfy` sits at `twist = 77.4°` (from `t3-prism-bo-batch-drop-results.csv`). The simulation disagrees with the bench on the twist axis, and `pr102_sim_campaign.md` section 4 attributes this to the model's inability to amplify (rigid struts, no bending modes).

---

## 5. All Simulation Observables — Computed vs. Screened

### Returned by `simulate()` (`drop_tower_sim.py` lines 330–355):

| Observable | Screened as objective? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `t180` | ✅ Primary objective | CFC-180 transmissibility |
| `e_rebound` | ✅ (dead) | Restitution velocity ratio; span <1% at fixed mass |
| `e_reb_mJ` | ✅ (dead) | `e_rebound × m × g × h`; = mass at fixed mass |
| `in_180_g` | ✅ Screened (null control) | Input peak; 0.1% span, mat-owned |
| `out_180_g` | ✅ Screened | rho vs t180 = 1.0 (duplicate) |
| `pulse_ms` | ✅ Screened (null control) | Input pulse width; 0.5% span, mat-owned |
| `t1000` | ✅ Screened | CFC-1000 transmissibility; rho vs t180 = 0.997 (near-duplicate) |
| `peak_tendon_strain` | ✅ Screened | Max TPU tension strain; span 63%, rho vs t180 = −0.41 |
| `peak_tendon_energy_mJ` | ✅ Screened | Peak elastic energy; span 157%, rho vs t180 = −0.87 |
| `stroke_mm` | ✅ Screened | Top-vertex compression; span 122%, rho vs t180 = −0.89 |
| `mass_printed_g` | Tracked metric | Fixed at 20.23 g on ratio manifold |
| `mass_flat_model_g` | Diagnostic | Flat-solidity mass estimate |
| `mass_solid_g` | Diagnostic | Solid-CAD mass |
| `tpu_fraction` | Diagnostic | TPU mass fraction |
| `v_rebound_mps` | Not screened | Raw rebound velocity |
| `print_scale` | Diagnostic | Uniform scale factor applied |
| `t` | Raw channel | Time array |
| `a_in_g`, `a_out_g` | Raw (CFC-180 filtered) | For plotting |
| `a_in_raw_g`, `a_out_raw_g` | Raw (unfiltered) | For ringdown fits |
| `v_car` | Raw channel | Carriage velocity |
| `f_mat` | Raw channel | Mat force |

### Computable but NOT screened:
1. **Modal frequency of the tendon network** (22–96 Hz in simulation) — computable from FFT of `a_out_raw_g` post-contact; not screened because it doesn't match the bench's 294–468 Hz strut-flexure modes (`zeta_analysis.md` section 3).
2. **Simulated ringdown damping ratio `zeta_pct`** — extractable from `a_out_raw_g - a_in_raw_g` post-contact; `zeta_analysis.md` shows it cannot be resolved (wrong mode family, parasitic damping floor, no cross-article signal).
3. **Impulse / delta-v of the mat contact** — integral of `f_mat` over time; directly computable from the `f_mat` array; not screened.
4. **Contact duration** — `(f_mat > 0).sum() * SIM_DT_S`; not screened.
5. **Peak mat force** — `f_mat.max()`; not screened separately from `in_180_g`.
6. **Per-tendon force time series** — `data.ten_length` is read per-step for strain; individual tendon forces are not stored or screened.
7. **Carriage rebound height** — `v_reb²/(2g)`; derivable from `v_rebound_mps`; not screened.
8. **CFC-60 transmissibility** — a lower-frequency filter than CFC-180; not computed.
9. **Relative acceleration peak** (`out_180_g - in_180_g`) — not screened; `out_180_g` alone is (but is a near-duplicate of `t180`).
10. **Energy balance**: input KE vs. rebound KE vs. mat dissipation — all components available from `v_car` and `f_mat`; not computed or screened.

---

## 6. Physical / Modeling Concerns (Flagged with Code Locations)

| # | Concern | Location |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Mat force law mislabeled**: implemented as `F = k·d − c·d·ż` (modified KV), not Hunt-Crossley `F = k·d^n(1+α·ż)`. At high ż, damping term can exceed stiffness term before the `max(...,0)` clip. | `drop_tower_sim.py` lines 261–265 |
| 2 | **Cable damping reference mass is the accelerometer (5 g)**, not the strut or modal mass. `c_cable` is therefore not physically grounded. | `drop_tower_sim.py` lines 186–187 |
| 3 | **Simulated `e_rebound` ≈ 0.61 vs. measured 0.02–0.05** (30× off). Calibration deliberately excludes restitution. Simulated `e_rebound` has <1% design response at fixed mass (rho vs `e_reb_mJ` = 0.026). | `pr102_sim_campaign.md` sections 1–2; `drop_tower_sim.py` `calibrate()` docstring |
| 4 | **Simulated `t180` cannot exceed 1** (rigid struts, no bending modes). Every tested article except `6lhxfy` shows amplification (t180 > 1) on the bench. Simulated S0 = 0.707 vs. measured 1.011. | `pr102_sim_campaign.md` section 2; `zeta_analysis.md` section 4 |
| 5 | **Twist optimum disagrees with bench**: simulation converges to 40° (lower bound); best bench article `6lhxfy` is at 77.4°. | `pr102_sim_campaign.md` section 4; `t3-prism-bo-batch-drop-results.csv` |
| 6 | **`in_180_g` (null control) ranks articles at rho = −0.89, p = 0.007** due to 0.09% numerical wobble from per-article mass differences. This is a spurious correlation from the mass-projection, not a physical signal. | `pr102_sim_campaign.md` section 3, point 3 |
| 7 | **Strut flexure entirely absent**: the 294–468 Hz ringdown band measured on the bench is strut bending; rigid capsules have no such modes. All modal observables from the simulation are in the 22–96 Hz rigid-body range. | `drop_tower_sim.py` docstring; `zeta_analysis.md` section 3 |
| 8 | **Tendon forces are nominal-stiffness proxies**, not constraint-solver forces: `ext = max(ten_length - rest_len, 0)`, `e = 0.5 * k_cable * sum(ext²)`. The MuJoCo tendon also carries a limit constraint at the same rest length, so the actual constraint force may differ. | `drop_tower_sim.py` lines 285–292 |
| 9 | **Parasitic damping floor at ~12% ζ** from equality-constraint stabilization and implicitfast integrator, independent of `cable_zeta`. This floors the emergent modal damping above the two least-damped bench articles (autv5r: 6.4%, 6lhxfy: 10.1%). | `zeta_analysis.md` section 3, point 3 |
| 10 | **`e_reb_mJ` is effectively mass** on the constant-solid-mass manifold (rho = 0.9999). The old projection was fatally flawed; the fix (constant printed mass) reduces this to rho = 0.997 but `e_rebound` still has only 0.5% design span. | `pr102_sim_campaign.md` section 1 |
| 11 | **`stroke_mm` and `peak_tendon_energy_mJ` have strong design response** (span 122% and 157%, rho vs t180 = −0.89 and −0.87) but were not promoted to campaign objectives. These are the best candidates for a second objective if the bench can measure article deformation. | `pr102_objective_screen_summary.csv`; `pr102_objective_screen.py` CANDIDATES dict |
| 12 | **`peak_tendon_strain`** has 63% span and rho vs t180 = −0.41 (genuinely independent), making it the most independent candidate with real design response — but it is a survivability proxy, not a performance metric, and was not screened against bench data. | `pr102_objective_screen_summary.csv` |

---

## Summary Table: Observable Screening Results

From `pr102_objective_screen_summary.csv` (128-point Sobol, ratio manifold):

| Candidate | Rel. span | ρ vs t180 | p | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `e_rebound` | 0.65% | +0.82 | 5.8e-20 | Dead: mat-owned, near-duplicate |
| `t1000` | 29.0% | +0.997 | 1.3e-83 | Dead: duplicate of t180 |
| `out_180_g` | 29.8% | +1.00 | 5.2e-165 | Dead: = t180 × in_180_g |
| `pulse_ms` | 0.49% | +0.47 | 1.1e-5 | Dead: mat-owned null control |
| `in_180_g` | 0.10% | −0.976 | 8.9e-52 | Dead: null control, numerical wobble |
| `peak_tendon_strain` | 63.1% | −0.41 | 2.3e-4 | **Candidate**: independent, survivability |
| `peak_tendon_energy_mJ` | 157.3% | −0.87 | 1.2e-25 | **Candidate**: strong response, correlated with t180 |
| `stroke_mm` | 121.7% | −0.89 | 1.1e-27 | **Candidate**: strong response, correlated with t180 |

**Not screened against bench data**: `peak_tendon_strain`, `peak_tendon_energy_mJ`, `stroke_mm`, `v_rebound_mps`, impulse, contact duration, per-tendon forces, energy balance, CFC-60 transmissibility, simulated `zeta_pct`.

## CSV Files Supporting Zeta Analysis and PR102 Correlation

### Exact Paths (all under `/workspace/`)

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `/workspace/t3-prism-bo-batch-drop-results.csv` | Bench drop-tower results for all 8–9 tested articles (101 drops each) |
| `/workspace/pr102_objective_screen.csv` | 128-point Sobol screen of all candidate second objectives on the constant-printed-mass ratio manifold |
| `/workspace/pr102_objective_screen_summary.csv` | Summary: per-candidate rel_span, rho vs t180, p-value, and per-axis sensitivities |

> **Note:** The `outputs/` directory referenced in `zeta_analysis.md` and `pr102_sim_campaign.md` does **not exist** on disk. The CSVs listed there (`outputs/zeta_measured_correlations.csv`, `outputs/zeta_articles_sim.csv`, `outputs/zeta_damping_transfer.csv`, `outputs/zeta_sobol_response.csv`, `outputs/zeta_article_inversion.csv`, `outputs/zeta_cross_checks.csv`, `outputs/pr102_reference_front.csv`, `outputs/pr102_baselines_summary.csv`, etc.) have **not been generated yet** — they are outputs of scripts not yet run.

---

### `/workspace/t3-prism-bo-batch-drop-results.csv` — Bench Results Schema

**Columns:** `specimen, n_valid, dv_health, t180_mean, t180_sd, t1000_mean, t1000_sd, out_180_g_mean, out_180_g_sd, in_180_g_mean, in_180_g_sd, in_dv_ms_mean, in_dv_ms_sd, t_second_ms_mean, t_second_ms_sd, e_rebound_mean, e_rebound_sd, fn_hz_mean, fn_hz_sd, zeta_pct_mean, zeta_pct_sd, H_mm, R_mm, cable_d_mm, mass_g, spec, strut_d_mm, twist_deg`

**Key results (9 articles, 101 drops each):**

| specimen | spec | dv_health | t180_mean | e_rebound_mean | zeta_pct_mean | fn_hz_mean | mass_g |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6lhxfy | 01 | healthy | **0.893** | 0.0504 | **10.15** | 368.4 | 18.5 |
| 6nheas | 05 | settled | 0.997 | 0.0402 | 19.31 | 322.0 | 21.73 |
| 9hhbkp | 00 | healthy | 1.018 | 0.0215 | 11.21 | 364.1 | 21.62 |
| amdjwm | — | settled | 0.980 | 0.0296 | 9.64 | 455.1 | — |
| autv5r | 02 | healthy | 1.040 | 0.0268 | **6.38** | 385.7 | 22.04 |
| bag26v | 08 | settled | 1.062 | 0.0241 | — | — | 21.42 |
| bpx68c | S0 | healthy | 1.011 | 0.0204 | 16.73 | 467.6 | 20.23 |
| nvxsrv | 04 | healthy | 1.028 | 0.0266 | **31.04** | 294.3 | 20.66 |

**Sim vs bench t180:** Simulated S0 (bpx68c) reads **0.707** vs measured **1.011** — the model can only attenuate (rigid struts, no bending modes), while every bench article except 6lhxfy shows amplification (t180 > 1). `e_rebound` measured 0.02–0.05 vs simulated ~0.61 (mat calibrated to input pulse, not restitution).

**Zeta (ringdown damping):** spans 6.4 % (autv5r) to 31.0 % (nvxsrv), ~4.9×. Within-article sd is 0.66–2.36 %, so between-article spread is ~7.5× the repeat noise. Measured ringdown frequencies: 294–468 Hz (strut flexure modes). Simulated ringdown frequencies: 22–96 Hz (rigid-body tendon modes) — the two clouds do not overlap.

---

### `/workspace/pr102_objective_screen.csv` — Sobol Screen Schema

**Columns (22 total):** `H_over_R, H_over_strut_d, cable_over_strut_d, twist_deg` (4 shape-ratio inputs) + `t180, e_rebound, e_reb_mJ, mass_g, print_scale, R_print_mm, H_print_mm, strut_d_print_mm, cable_d_print_mm, envelope_cm3, t1000, peak_tendon_strain, peak_tendon_energy_mJ, stroke_mm, in_180_g, out_180_g, pulse_ms, feasible`

128 Sobol designs on the constant-printed-mass (20.23 g) ratio manifold; ~40% infeasible (cable/envelope constraints). All `mass_g` = 20.23 g (fixed by projection).

---

### `/workspace/pr102_objective_screen_summary.csv` — Candidate Second Objectives

**Schema:** `candidate, rel_span, rho_vs_t180, p, meaning, rho_H_over_R, rho_H_over_strut_d, rho_cable_over_strut_d, rho_twist_deg`

| candidate | rel_span | rho_vs_t180 | p | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **e_rebound** | 0.0065 | +0.818 | 5.8e-20 | Restitution ratio (being replaced) — near-duplicate of t180, dead as 2nd obj |
| **t1000** | 0.290 | **+0.997** | 1.3e-83 | CFC-1000 transmissibility — essentially identical to t180, useless as 2nd obj |
| **out_180_g** | 0.298 | **+1.000** | 5.2e-165 | Absolute filtered peak at top vertex — perfectly correlated with t180 |
| **pulse_ms** | 0.0049 | +0.475 | 1.1e-5 | Input pulse width — mat-owned null control, tiny span |
| **in_180_g** | 0.0010 | -0.976 | 8.9e-52 | Input peak — mat-owned null control, 0.1% span (numerical noise) |
| **peak_tendon_strain** | **0.631** | -0.406 | 2.3e-4 | Max TPU tension strain — large span, moderate independence; survivability metric |
| **peak_tendon_energy_mJ** | **1.573** | -0.875 | 1.2e-25 | Peak elastic energy in tendon network — large span but strongly anti-correlated with t180 |
| **stroke_mm** | **1.217** | -0.890 | 1.1e-27 | Max top-vertex compression — large span but strongly anti-correlated with t180 |

**Key axis sensitivities for top candidates:**
- `peak_tendon_strain`: driven by `cable_over_strut_d` (rho = -0.764) — thinner cables → higher strain
- `peak_tendon_energy_mJ`: driven by `H_over_R` (rho = -0.917) — flatter cells store less tendon energy
- `stroke_mm`: driven by `H_over_R` (rho = -0.835) — flatter cells compress less

---

### Key Findings Relevant to Each Topic

**Mat loss / damping injection:**
- The calibrated Hunt-Crossley PU mat owns essentially all of the loss budget. Injecting article damping via `cable_zeta` changes simulated `t180` by median 0.12% (max 3.9%) and `e_rebound` by median 0.009% (max 0.12%). This is a **missing-mechanism problem**, not a calibration problem.
- Simulated `e_rebound` ≈ 0.61 vs measured 0.02–0.05; the gap is energy leaving through guide rails, anvil, and frame — paths absent from the model.

**Zeta / damping injection failure (4 independent failures):**
1. Wrong mode family: sim 22–96 Hz vs bench 294–468 Hz
2. No cross-article signal: Spearman(sim ζ, measured ζ) = -0.54 (n=6, p=0.27) — zero signal
3. Damping floor ~12% pins above the best articles (autv5r at 6.4%, 6lhxfy at 10.1%)
4. Design response is mode-structure noise: sim ζ spans 7–79% with max |rho| = 0.21 across 48 Sobol designs

**Sim vs bench t180/rebound:**
- Best simulated predictor of measured t180: `lander_SEA_J_per_cm3` (rho = -0.93, p = 0.003, rel_span 231%) — a Tier-C structural energy density observable, not the drop-tower analogue itself
- `sim_t180` itself: rho = +0.50 (p = 0.25) — not significant
- Measured `e_reb_mJ`: best predictor `lander_eta` at rho = +0.82 (p = 0.023) but on 0.12% span (numerical noise); no usable simulated predictor exists

**Candidate second objectives:**
- `e_rebound`, `t1000`, `out_180_g`: all disqualified — rho vs t180 ≥ 0.82, front collapses to a sliver

- Recommended from correlation study: `SEA_J_per_cm3` (lander regime, rho = -0.93 vs measured t180, rel_span 231%) as the GP surrogate input, pending perturbation testing

from itertools import permutations

def spearman_exact_p(x,y):

55d13aec Replaced the per-step sparse Cholesky factorization of the flex block of the implicit effective metric M + K with its prefactored per-vertex 3x3 diagonal blocks. The blocks precondition the CG constraint solver and drive an iterative solve for`qacc_smooth`, which now converges on tolerance rather than a fixed threshold. Flexes with elastic2d stretch stiffness step roughly twice as fast; bending-only flexes keep the exact constant factor and are unchanged.

431→1. **The surrogate is what is doing the work, not the space-filling design.**
432→   The BO's first nine designs *are* a Sobol batch (Ax's own generator, a
433→   different scramble from the `sobol` baseline's, hence the small offset at
434→   design 9: 9.25 against 9.81, with the baseline slightly ahead). The moment
435→   the model takes over the traces separate and never re-cross: one
436→   model-driven batch takes the BO from 51 % of the reference ceiling to
437→   83 %, and it is at 96 % by design 18 and 97 % by design 27. Sobol run out
438→   to the full 36 designs finishes at 66 %. Space filling is not the
439→   ingredient.
440→2. **Sobol and LHS are indistinguishable from each other, and barely beat
441→   random.** 65.6 % against 64.7 % against 60.3 %, with sd of 1.1 to 1.5. At
442→   36 points in 5 dimensions, quasi-random stratification buys very little.
443→3. **The heuristic is the strongest baseline and still loses by a wide
444→   margin**, and it has the largest seed-to-seed spread of any method
445→   (sd 1.78, and 4.04 mJ on best `e_reb_mJ`). That is the expected signature
446→   of a local method on a front whose extremes are box corners: whether a run
447→   ends up near one depends on where it started.
448→
449→The BO's spread is also the smallest of the five (sd 0.25 = 1.4 % of its
450→mean, against 9 to 12 % for the baselines). Across ten independent repeats it
451→is both better and more repeatable, which is the property that matters when
452→each real evaluation is a print plus a drop session.
453→
454→![objective space](outputs/pr102_baselines_objective_space.png)
455→
456→Pooled over ten seeds, the BO's points lie along the front; every baseline's
457→points are a cloud in the interior. Note the BO does *not* reach the extreme
458→low-`e_reb_mJ` tail of the front, which lives at `R` 25 / `H` 110 /
459→`strut_d` 12: qNEHVI spends its budget on the knee, which is where
460→hypervolume is, and the tail is worth about 1 mJ.
461→
462→### Caveat on all of the above
463→
464→This compares optimizers on a **simulated** objective, so what it measures is
465→search efficiency on this response surface, not accuracy against the bench.
466→Section 3's caveats still apply to the objective itself. The transfer that
467→does hold is the shape of the problem: 5 continuous axes, 2 objectives,
468→a smooth deterministic response, a front on the box boundary. On that shape,
469→36 model-driven evaluations reach 97 % of a 68,944-evaluation ceiling and 36
470→space-filling ones reach 66 %.
471→
472→Files. `outputs/pr102_reference_cloud.csv.gz` (all 68,944 evaluations,
473→gzipped, read directly by pandas), `outputs/pr102_reference_front.csv` (the
474→247 non-dominated designs), `outputs/pr102_reference_summary.csv`,
475→`outputs/pr102_baseline_<strategy>_seed<k>.csv` (40 runs, every evaluation
476→with its parameters, objectives, printed mass, constant-mass scale and
477→feasibility flag), `outputs/pr102_baselines_summary.csv`, and the two
478→figures. Nothing needs re-running to redo a plot.
479→
480→## 6. The campaign on the constant-mass shape-ratio manifold
481→
482→The 2026-08-22 review of the slab runs recommended re-parameterizing
483→instead of carrying mass as a parameter: in a deterministic simulation mass
484→is a function of shape, so a mass axis is degenerate (every point shares
485→its projected article with a one-parameter family of others) and the slab
486→is exploitable as a gradient, which is exactly how all ten slab repeats
487→used it. `--space ratios`, now the default, implements that
488→recommendation.
489→
490→The search space is the four dimensionless shape ratios, `H/R` in [1.5,
491→4.4], `H/strut_d` in [5, 18.3], `cable_d/strut_d` in [0.25, 0.917] and
492→`twist` in [40, 80] deg, the extremes the PR #35 box can express. The
493→single overall scale is solved in closed form by the section 1 mass model
494→so every evaluated article prints at exactly 20.23 g; mass never enters
495→the search space, and the second objective becomes the dimensionless
496→`e_rebound` (`e_reb_mJ` is the constant `m* g h` times it on this
497→manifold). What the base box can no longer police is printability, so it
498→enters honestly instead of implicitly: the projected article's cable
499→diameter (3.0 mm TPU bridging floor) and envelope (250 cm^3) are Ax
500→outcome constraints under constrained qNEHVI, and they bind, on about 40 %
501→of the ratio box (unprintable projections are excluded from every front,
502→hypervolume and running best below, but kept in the CSVs).
503→
504→### Ten repeats, reference, baselines
505→
506→The same construction as sections 4 and 5, re-run end to end on the new
507→manifold: ten from-scratch repeats (`--model botorch`, `--init sobol`,
508→five batches of 9 = 45 designs each), a reference sweep (16,384 scrambled
509→Sobol designs plus the 21-weighting Nelder-Mead polish, 21,184 evaluations,
510→about 470x the campaign budget), and the four baselines at the campaign's
511→budget over the same ten seeds.
512→
513→![](outputs/pr102_sim_bo_botorch_ratios_sobol_aggregate.png)
514→
515→The repeats start far apart (round-0 hypervolume spread 24.9 % of its
516→mean, best round-0 `t180` 0.651 to 0.790) and finish close (final
517→hypervolume 0.00978 +/- 0.00027, 2.9 % of the mean, best `t180` 0.589 to
518→0.599 for nine of ten seeds): convergent under resampling, without the
519→degenerate identical-vertex collapse of the slab space. One seed (6) stalls
520→at `t180` 0.619 with its twist at 63 deg, the price of a 45-design budget
521→on a constrained space, and it is visible rather than averaged away.
522→
523→| method | final HV (mean +/- sd) | fraction of reference | best `t180` (mean) | p vs BO |
524→|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
525→| BO (constrained qNEHVI) | 0.00978 +/- 0.00027 | **95.2 %** | 0.597 | - |
526→| Latin hypercube | 0.00748 +/- 0.00074 | 72.7 % | 0.661 | 9.1e-5 |
527→| Sobol | 0.00703 +/- 0.00119 | 68.4 % | 0.674 | 1.2e-4 |
528→| compass search | 0.00685 +/- 0.00273 | 66.6 % | 0.680 | 3.6e-3 |
529→| random search | 0.00669 +/- 0.00176 | 65.0 % | 0.684 | 9.1e-5 |
530→
531→![](outputs/pr102_baselines_comparison_ratios.png)
532→
533→The BO's margin survives the re-parameterization, and one baseline moved in
534→an informative way: compass search, the strongest baseline on the
535→unconstrained slab (80 % of reference), drops to the bottom of the pack
536→here, because roughly a third of its probe moves land on unprintable
537→projections that a penalty can reject but not steer around. A model that
538→learns the constraint surfaces loses much less of its budget to them.
539→
540→### Where the optimum moved, and what binds now
541→
542→![](outputs/pr102_reference_front_ratios.png)
543→
544→* **The envelope constraint replaces the box wall.** Nine of ten repeat
545→  winners and 98.7 % of the 555-point reference front press the 250 cm^3
546→  envelope cap (those winners at 245 to 249 cm^3), and the front's
547→  best-`t180` end sits on
548→  the cable print floor at exactly 3.00 mm as well. On the slab space the
549→  answer was "sit in the corner of the box"; here it is "print the widest,
550→  flattest cell the build volume and the bridging floor allow at 20.23 g",
551→  which is a statement about the printer and the physics rather than about
552→  where someone drew the search box.
553→* **`H/R` and `twist` still sit on their bounds** (1.5 and 40 deg across
554→  the front and nine of ten winners). Those walls came from the PR #35 box
555→  extremes, so the earlier conclusion survives re-parameterization: the
556→  next plate is worth more below `twist` 40 deg and below `H/R` 1.5, in
557→  other words flatter and wider than the current family allows.
558→* **The winning printed article** is R about 37.5 mm, H about 56 mm, strut
559→  6.3 to 10.6 mm, cable 3.4 to 4.6 mm, `t180` about 0.59 against the
560→  reference's 0.5825. The strut-diameter axis stays soft: `H/strut_d`
561→  from 5.2 to 8.9 all reach `t180` within 1 %, so the model is trading it
562→  against cable ratio along a shallow valley, consistent with the front
563→  geometry panel, where the trade-off is carried entirely by
564→  `cable_d/strut_d` and `H/strut_d`.
565→* **The two objectives are now largely concordant, not competing.** Over
566→  the 13,937 printable reference designs `e_rebound` spans 0.71 % and
567→  rank-correlates with `t180` at rho = +0.84, so the Pareto front is a
568→  sliver (its `t180` extent is 0.5825 to 0.5995) and the campaign is
569→  effectively single-objective in `t180`. That is the section 1 finding
570→  surviving one more reformulation, now with nothing left to hide behind:
571→  the simulated restitution has no design response at fixed mass, and a
572→  live second objective needs either a tier that carries the rig's loss
573→  paths or the bench itself.
574→
575→Files. `outputs/pr102_sim_bo_botorch_ratios_sobol_seed<k>.{csv,png}`,
576→`..._aggregate.png`, `..._summary.csv`;
577→`outputs/pr102_reference_{cloud,front,summary}_ratios.*`;
578→`outputs/pr102_baseline_<strategy>_ratios_seed<k>.csv`;
579→`outputs/pr102_baselines_{comparison,objective_space,summary}_ratios.*`.
580→Every evaluation is on disk, printable or not, so any of this can be
581→re-plotted without re-running.
582→

587→  hypothesis to test on the next batch, not as an established transfer
588→  function.
589→* `lander_eta`'s 0.13 percent span has not been perturbation-tested (vary

info.name: run_cell
info.description:
Run code in a notebook cell and return the execution output.

This method allows running code in a new cell (append) or re-running
an existing cell with updated code.

Usage Examples:
    run_cell("print('Hello, world!')",
            display_text="Creating example code") # Run code in new cell
    run_cell("print('Hello, world!')",
            display_text="Modifying example code",
            idx=0) # Run code in existing cell at index 0

Error Recovery:
    When a cell fails with an error, you MUST fix it by calling run_cell
    with the corrected code and the SAME idx as the failed cell:

    run_cell("corrected_code", idx=3)  # Fix error in Cell #3

    The cell number is shown in the output prefix (e.g., "[Cell #3]").
    Do NOT create a new cell to fix an error - always edit the failed cell.

display_text.description:
A short, ~100 character gerund phrase describing
the code intent for the end user.
display_text.title: Display Text

idx.description:
Cell index to run. If None or >= len(cells), appends a new cell.
If provided, updates and re-runs the existing cell at that index.
Use this to fix errors in existing cells.
idx.title: Idx

info.name: explore
info.description:
Search the workspace or memory for information.

Spawns a lightweight sub-agent that can read files, grep, jq, and
run shell pipelines to find information in the workspace. Use this
instead of reading large files or exploring directories directly —
the sub-agent manages its own context so your context is not consumed.

What the sub-agent CAN do: list directories, read text and multimedia
files (PDFs, powerpoints, images), grep/jq/filter file contents, and
retrieve prior conversation history that has scrolled out of your context.

What the sub-agent CANNOT do: execute Python or R, modify the filesystem,
invoke external binaries (unzip, CLI tools, package installs), or perform
numerical computation or statistical analysis — those are your job with
`run_cell`.

Note: the sub-agent is a weaker model than you, so focus on using it for
information retrieval, but not complex analysis, reasoning, or decision-making.
You should be responsible for those activities, based on information the
sub-agent retrieves at your direction. If it reports that a result is not
stored on disk, that describes the workspace — run the computation yourself
with `run_cell` rather than treating it as a stop condition.

Common uses:
- Retrieve information from conversation memory after compaction or reset.
- Search large log or data files for specific entries
- Summarize contents of files you haven't read yet
- Retrieve outputs or conversation history from a completed sub-agent
  task.
